pages.title: Sympathy Card Messages for a Coworker
pages.metaTitle: Sympathy Card Messages for a Coworker | Prosepal
pages.metaDescription: Find thoughtful sympathy card messages for a coworker. 10 examples plus tips for expressing condolences professionally and genuinely.
pages.intro: Writing a sympathy card for a coworker requires a delicate balance. You want to be genuine and supportive, but also respectful of professional boundaries. The relationship you have at work is different from personal friendships, yet moments of loss transcend those boundaries. Here's how to find the right words.

tips.title: Keep It Professional but Warm
tips.content: You don't need to share deeply personal sentiments. Focus on acknowledging their loss and offering practical support, like covering their workload while they're away.

tips.title: Don't Assume You Know Their Grief
tips.content: Avoid phrases like "I know how you feel" even if you've experienced loss. Everyone's grief is unique. Instead, simply acknowledge that this is a difficult time.

tips.title: Offer Specific Help
tips.content: Rather than "Let me know if you need anything," offer something concrete: "I'll handle the Henderson account while you're out" or "I'll make sure you don't come back to a full inbox."

shortMessages: Thinking of you during this difficult time. Please don't worry about anything here—we've got you covered.
I'm so sorry for your loss. Take all the time you need.
My deepest condolences. Wishing you strength and peace.
mediumMessages: I was so sorry to hear about your loss. Please know that we're all thinking of you and your family. Take whatever time you need—everything here will be handled.
My heart goes out to you during this difficult time. I can only imagine how hard this must be. Please don't hesitate to reach out if there's anything I can do.
I want you to know how sorry I am for your loss. When you're ready to come back, we'll all be here. Until then, focus on yourself and your family.
heartfeltMessages: I don't have the right words—no one does for something like this. I just want you to know that I'm here, the team is here, and we're all holding space for you. Take care of yourself.
Losing someone you love changes everything. I'm so deeply sorry you're going through this. Please know that you don't have to face any of this alone—not here, not anywhere. We're all thinking of you.
I wish I could do more than send words, but please know they come with genuine care. Your [loved one] was lucky to have you. Take all the time you need—we'll be here when you're ready.
There's nothing I can say to make this easier, and I won't try to. Just know that my thoughts are with you, and the whole team is ready to support you however we can.
pages.whenToSend: Send your sympathy card as soon as you learn of the loss—ideally within a few days. If your coworker is out of the office, you can mail it to their home address (if known and appropriate) or leave it with HR to forward. Consider signing a group card from the team as well as sending a personal note if you're close.

faqs.question: Should I mention the deceased by name?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you knew their name. Using the name of the person who passed shows you care and makes the message more personal. If you didn't know the person, "your loved one" or "your [mother/father/etc.]" works well.

faqs.question: Is it appropriate to send flowers to a coworker?
faqs.answer: Flowers are generally appropriate, especially from a team or department. Individual flowers are also fine if you're close. Check with HR or the coworker's close friends about any preferences or cultural considerations.

faqs.question: What if I didn't know them well?
faqs.answer: That's okay—your card can be brief. Even a short note saying "I'm sorry for your loss. Thinking of you." shows you care. You don't need a deep relationship to offer genuine condolences.

pages.title: Sympathy Card Messages for a Friend
pages.metaTitle: Sympathy Card Messages for a Friend | Prosepal
pages.metaDescription: Find heartfelt sympathy card messages for a friend. 10 examples plus tips for expressing genuine condolences during their time of loss.
pages.intro: When your friend loses someone they love, you want to say something that actually helps—not just fill the blank space in a card. But finding those words is hard. Your friend doesn't need platitudes; they need to know you're there. Here's how to write something real.

tips.title: Be Honest About the Difficulty
tips.content: It's okay to acknowledge that you don't have the right words. Saying "I don't know what to say, but I'm here" is more powerful than forced eloquence.

tips.title: Make a Specific Offer
tips.content: "I'm bringing dinner Thursday" is better than "Let me know if you need anything." Grieving people rarely reach out for help, so be specific and proactive.

tips.title: Share a Memory If You Have One
tips.content: If you knew the person who passed, sharing a specific memory can be incredibly meaningful. It shows their loved one's impact extended beyond immediate family.

shortMessages: I'm so sorry. I'm here—for whatever you need, whenever you need it.
My heart is with you. I love you and I'm not going anywhere.
There are no words. Just know I'm here.
mediumMessages: I've been thinking about you constantly. There's nothing I can say to make this better, but I want you to know I'm here. Call me at 3am if you need to. I mean it.
I'm so deeply sorry for your loss. [Name] was such a light, and I know how much they meant to you. I'm bringing dinner over Thursday—no need to reply.
Losing someone you love this much is devastating. I won't pretend to understand your pain, but I'll sit with you in it for as long as you need.
heartfeltMessages: I don't have the right words, and I'm not going to pretend I do. I'm just here—for the hard days, the quiet ones, and whenever you need someone to sit with you in this. Love you.
[Name] was one of the good ones. I'll never forget [specific memory]. I know nothing I say can ease this pain, but I hope you know how loved you are—by them, and by me.
I wish I could take some of this pain away from you. Since I can't, I'll just be here—to listen, to sit in silence, to bring wine, whatever you need. You're not alone in this.
My heart is broken for you. [Name] raised an incredible person, and their legacy lives on in you. I'm here for whatever comes next—today, next month, next year.
pages.whenToSend: Send your sympathy card as soon as you hear the news—ideally within the first week. Don't wait for the "perfect" moment or message. Your friend needs to know you're thinking of them now, not just at the funeral. Consider following up with a call or visit in the weeks after, when others have moved on but grief remains.

faqs.question: What if I didn't know the person who passed?
faqs.answer: That's okay. Focus on your friend and their loss: "I never had the chance to meet your mom, but from everything you've shared, she sounded incredible. I'm so sorry for your loss."

faqs.question: Should I avoid talking about the loss?
faqs.answer: No—most grieving people want to talk about their loved one. Don't avoid the topic out of fear of "making them sad." They're already sad. Your acknowledgment helps.

faqs.question: How do I follow up after the card?
faqs.answer: Check in regularly—not just the first week. Text or call in the weeks and months after. Mark the anniversary on your calendar and reach out then too.

pages.title: Sympathy Card Messages for Loss of a Parent

pages.metaDescription: Find thoughtful condolence messages for someone who lost a parent. 10 examples plus tips for expressing sympathy for the loss of a mother or father.
pages.intro: Losing a parent changes everything. Whether it was expected or sudden, whether the relationship was close or complicated—the loss of a mother or father is profound. Your words won't fix their grief, but they can offer comfort. Here's how to write something meaningful.

tips.title: Acknowledge the Unique Bond
tips.content: The parent-child relationship is unlike any other. Recognize this: "The bond between a parent and child is irreplaceable" validates the depth of their loss.

tips.title: Mention Qualities You Admired
tips.content: If you knew the parent, share what you admired about them. If not, mention qualities you see in your friend that likely came from their parent.

tips.title: Avoid Minimizing the Loss
tips.content: Skip phrases like "at least they lived a long life" or "they're in a better place." Even well-intended words can feel dismissive. Focus on acknowledging their pain.

shortMessages: I'm so sorry for the loss of your [mom/dad]. Holding you in my heart.
There are no words for losing a parent. I'm here for you.
Sending you love and strength during this impossibly hard time.
mediumMessages: I'm so deeply sorry for the loss of your [mother/father]. The love between a parent and child is something sacred, and I know this loss is immeasurable.
Your [mom/dad] raised someone incredible—you. That legacy lives on. I'm so sorry they're gone, and I'm here for whatever you need.
Losing a parent changes everything. I won't pretend to know what you're going through, but I want you to know I'm thinking of you and I'm here.
heartfeltMessages: I'm so sorry for the loss of your [mom/dad]. From everything you've shared about them, they were truly one of a kind. The world—and your life—was better for having them in it.

There's no preparing for losing a parent. Even when we know it's coming, the reality hits differently. I'm holding space for you through all of this—the grief, the memories, the good days and the impossibly hard ones.
Your [mom/dad] clearly did something right—just look at who you've become. I wish I had better words, but please know my heart is with yours right now.
[Name] was such a light in your life, and I know that light will never fully go out. But I also know how dark things must feel right now. I'm here—not with answers, just with love.
pages.whenToSend: Send your sympathy card within the first week of learning about the loss. If you're attending the funeral or memorial, you can bring the card with you or send it separately. Consider reaching out again around significant dates—the first birthday without them, Mother's Day or Father's Day, and the one-year anniversary.

faqs.question: What if they had a complicated relationship with their parent?
faqs.answer: Grief is complicated even in difficult relationships. Keep your message simple and focused on your friend: "I'm here for you during this difficult time." Don't make assumptions about how they "should" feel.

faqs.question: Should I share my own experience losing a parent?
faqs.answer: Only briefly, if at all. A quick mention that you understand loss can help, but avoid making it about you. Their grief is the focus right now.

faqs.question: How do I address the card if both parents passed?
faqs.answer: If both parents passed close together (or at the same time), acknowledge both: "I'm so deeply sorry for the loss of your parents. I can't imagine facing this double grief."

pages.title: Birthday Card Messages for Mom

pages.metaDescription: Find heartfelt birthday card messages for mom. 10 examples from sweet to funny, plus tips for writing something she'll actually treasure.
pages.intro: Your mom has probably kept every card you've ever given her. So when her birthday comes around, "Happy Birthday Mom!" followed by awkward blank space doesn't quite cut it. She deserves something that captures even a fraction of what she means to you. Here's how to write it.

tips.title: Get Specific
tips.content: Instead of generic praise, mention something specific: a piece of advice she gave you, a memory you treasure, or a quality you've inherited from her.

tips.title: Match Her Personality
tips.content: Is your mom sentimental or does she prefer humor? Write to who she is. A joking mom might appreciate wit; a sentimental mom will treasure heartfelt words.

tips.title: Thank Her for Something Real
tips.content: Go beyond "thanks for everything." Thank her for something specific: the late-night talks, the way she always believes in you, the recipe she passed down.

shortMessages: Happy birthday to the woman who made me who I am. Love you more than words can say.
Mom, you make everything better. Hope your day is as wonderful as you are.
Another year of being the best mom ever. Happy birthday!
mediumMessages: Happy birthday, Mom. You've given me so much—your strength, your kindness, your terrible jokes. I'm grateful for all of it (even the jokes). Have the best day.
Mom, I don't tell you enough how much you mean to me. You're my first call when something goes wrong and my first call when something goes right. Happy birthday to my favorite person.
Every good thing about me came from you. Well, the good things anyway—we can blame Dad for the rest. Happy birthday, Mom. You deserve the world.
heartfeltMessages: Mom, there's no card big enough for everything I want to say. You've been my biggest supporter, my voice of reason, and my safe place my entire life. I hope you know how much that means to me. Happy birthday—I love you endlessly.
As I get older, I understand more and more what you sacrificed to give me everything. I'll never be able to repay you, but I hope I make you proud. Happy birthday to the strongest woman I know.

You taught me what it means to love unconditionally, to show up even when it's hard, and to always have snacks in my purse. I'm the person I am because of you. Happy birthday, Mom. I love you more than I could ever put into words.
Some people never get to know what it feels like to have a mom like you. I got lucky. Thank you for being exactly who you are—funny, fierce, and always in my corner. Happy birthday.
pages.whenToSend: Birthday cards should arrive on or before the birthday. If mailing, send at least a week early. If you're seeing her in person, bring the card to your celebration. Consider pairing it with something personal—a photo from your childhood, a gift card to her favorite place, or a promise of quality time together.

faqs.question: What if my relationship with my mom is complicated?
faqs.answer: Keep it simple and focus on something true: "Happy birthday, Mom. Thinking of you today." You don't have to fabricate emotions you don't feel, but acknowledging the day can still be meaningful.

faqs.question: How do I write a card for a milestone birthday (50, 60, 70)?
faqs.answer: Milestone birthdays deserve extra reflection. Consider looking back on memories from different decades, or acknowledging the wisdom and strength she's gained over the years.

faqs.question: Should I write a birthday card for my mother-in-law?
faqs.answer: Yes! A thoughtful note to your mother-in-law shows you value your relationship with her. Keep it warm and appreciative: "Thank you for raising someone I love so much."

pages.metaDescription: Find heartfelt birthday card messages for dad. 10 examples from funny to sincere, plus tips for writing something he'll remember.
pages.intro: Dads are notoriously hard to write cards for. He'll probably say "you didn't have to get me anything," but we both know he'll keep that card in his desk drawer for years. Here's how to write something worth keeping.

tips.title: Remember Dads Have Feelings Too
tips.content: Even if your dad isn't outwardly emotional, a genuine message means more than you might think. Don't default to humor if what you really want to say is heartfelt.

tips.title: Acknowledge Something Specific
tips.content: Reference a specific memory, lesson, or quality. "Thanks for teaching me to change a tire" lands better than "thanks for everything."

tips.title: Match His Communication Style
tips.content: If your dad jokes around, feel free to be funny. If he's more serious, go sincere. The best card sounds like something you'd actually say to him.

shortMessages: Happy birthday, Dad. Still the best advice-giver, bad-joke-teller, and father I could ask for.
To the man who taught me everything (except how to be brief). Happy birthday!
Dad, thanks for always being in my corner. Happy birthday to the best.
mediumMessages: Happy birthday, Dad. As I've gotten older, I've realized how much of who I am came from you—the good stuff, anyway. Thanks for being my first hero and my forever role model.
Dad, you've always been there—for the big moments and the boring ones. I hope you know how much that means. Happy birthday to the guy who makes it all look easy.
Remember when you used to let me "help" with projects even though I was definitely making it harder? That patience defines who you are. Happy birthday, Dad.
heartfeltMessages: Dad, I know you're not big on cards. But I wanted you to know that I see everything you've done for our family, even the stuff you don't think anyone notices. You're the reason I know what a good man looks like. Happy birthday.
Growing up, I wanted to be just like you. Now that I'm older, I realize what a high bar that was. Thank you for showing me what hard work, integrity, and love look like. Happy birthday, Dad.
You never missed a game, a recital, or a chance to tell me you were proud. I didn't know how rare that was until I grew up. Happy birthday to the best dad anyone could ask for.
Dad, you've given me so much—your work ethic, your sense of humor, your questionable taste in music. I wouldn't trade any of it. Happy birthday. I love you more than I say.
pages.whenToSend: Make sure your card arrives on or before his birthday. If you're seeing him in person, bring it to the celebration. For Father's Day dads, don't skip the birthday card just because another card holiday is coming—he deserves both.

faqs.question: What if I'm not close with my dad?
faqs.answer: Keep it simple and polite: "Happy birthday, Dad. Hope you have a great day." You don't need to pretend a closeness that doesn't exist, but acknowledging the day is still appropriate.

faqs.question: How do I write a card for my stepdad?
faqs.answer: Acknowledge his role in your life: "You didn't have to step up, but you did. Thank you for being the dad you didn't have to be. Happy birthday." Be genuine about your appreciation.

faqs.question: What about a dad who's hard to shop for?
faqs.answer: A heartfelt card often means more than a physical gift. Consider pairing it with quality time: "Your gift this year is an afternoon doing whatever you want—your choice."

pages.intro: Writing a thank you card to your boss walks a fine line: you want to express genuine gratitude without coming across as a brownnoser. Whether they gave you a raise, supported your growth, or just made work less terrible—here's how to say thank you the right way.

tips.title: Be Specific About What You're Thankful For
tips.content: "Thank you for being a great boss" is vague. "Thank you for advocating for my promotion" or "Thank you for mentoring me on the Johnson project" shows you mean it.

tips.title: Keep It Professional
tips.content: This isn't the place for inside jokes or overly casual language. Warm but professional is the sweet spot. Save the buddy-buddy stuff for happy hour.

tips.title: Acknowledge Their Impact
tips.content: Good bosses often don't hear how much they matter. Let them know how their leadership has affected your work or career growth.

shortMessages: Thank you for your support and leadership. It makes all the difference.
I'm grateful to have a boss who actually cares about their team. Thank you.
Thank you for believing in me—it means more than you know.
mediumMessages: I wanted to take a moment to thank you for everything you do for our team. Your leadership and support have made a real impact on my work and my growth here.
Thank you for [specific thing—the raise, the opportunity, the mentorship]. I don't take it for granted, and I'm grateful to work with someone who invests in their team.
Working under your leadership has taught me so much. Thank you for creating an environment where I can grow and do my best work.
heartfeltMessages: I've had bosses before, but I've never had a leader like you. Thank you for pushing me to be better while also having my back. It's rare, and I don't take it for granted.
When I look back on this chapter of my career, you'll be someone I remember. Thank you for the mentorship, the opportunities, and for being someone I genuinely respect. It means everything.
Thank you for seeing potential in me that I didn't always see in myself. Your belief in my abilities has pushed me to grow in ways I didn't think possible. I'm incredibly grateful.
A good boss makes a good job great. Thank you for being that person—for our whole team, and especially for me. Your leadership doesn't go unnoticed.
pages.whenToSend: Send a thank you card shortly after the event you're grateful for—within a week of a raise, promotion, or significant support. For general appreciation, Boss's Day (October 16) or year-end are appropriate times. Handwritten notes often feel more genuine than digital messages in professional settings.

faqs.question: Is it appropriate to give a gift with the card?
faqs.answer: A small, thoughtful gift is fine for significant occasions (a promotion they championed, for example). For everyday appreciation, the card alone is appropriate. Avoid anything too expensive or personal.

faqs.question: What if my relationship with my boss is strictly professional?
faqs.answer: That's fine—keep the card professional too. Focus on their leadership qualities and specific ways they've supported the team or your work.

faqs.question: Should the whole team sign one card or should I send my own?
faqs.answer: Both are appropriate. A team card shows collective appreciation; a personal card shows individual initiative. For significant personal support, a separate card is more meaningful.

pages.intro: Teachers change lives, but they rarely hear about it. Whether it's your child's teacher, your own teacher from years past, or a mentor who shaped your path—a genuine thank you card can mean more than you realize. Here's how to write one that actually says something.

tips.title: Be Specific About Their Impact
tips.content: "You're a great teacher" is nice but forgettable. "You made me love reading" or "You're the reason I became an engineer" is something they'll remember.

tips.title: Include a Concrete Example
tips.content: Reference a specific moment, lesson, or piece of advice that stuck with you. These details show your gratitude is genuine, not generic.

tips.title: Let Them Know It Lasted
tips.content: Teachers often wonder if they made a difference. Telling them how their influence shaped you beyond the classroom is incredibly meaningful.

shortMessages: Thank you for making a difference. Your impact will stay with me forever.
You made learning feel exciting. Thank you for being an incredible teacher.
Thank you for believing in me—it changed everything.
mediumMessages: I wanted to take a moment to thank you for everything you've done this year. Your patience, creativity, and dedication don't go unnoticed. [Child's name] is so lucky to have you.
Thank you for being the kind of teacher who actually cares. You made a real difference in my life, and I'll always be grateful for that.
Years later, I still think about the lessons you taught me—and not just the academic ones. Thank you for being the teacher you didn't have to be.
heartfeltMessages: I don't know if you realize the impact you've had on me. You saw something in me I didn't see in myself, and you refused to let me give up. I wouldn't be where I am today without you. Thank you.
Great teachers don't just teach subjects—they teach people. You taught me to think critically, to believe in myself, and to never stop asking questions. I carry those lessons with me every day.
Thank you for creating a classroom where it was safe to fail, to ask questions, and to be curious. That kind of environment is rare, and it changed my relationship with learning forever.

You probably don't remember this, but [specific moment]. That one interaction changed the trajectory of my life. Thank you for being the teacher who showed up—not just for the curriculum, but for the students.
pages.whenToSend: End of the school year and Teacher Appreciation Week (first full week of May) are perfect times. But any time you feel gratitude—even years later—is appropriate. Former students reaching out years after graduating often means the most to teachers.

faqs.question: Should I include a gift?
faqs.answer: Gifts are nice but not necessary. If you want to include something, gift cards (coffee shops, bookstores, school supply stores) or something personal based on their interests are appreciated. But the heartfelt note is what they'll keep.

faqs.question: What if my child is writing the card?
faqs.answer: Let your child's voice shine through! Their genuine, sometimes imperfect words often mean more than polished adult prose. You can help them express specific things they appreciate.

faqs.question: Is it okay to thank a teacher from years ago?
faqs.answer: Absolutely—these cards are often the most meaningful. Teachers spend years wondering if they made a difference. Hearing from a former student confirms that they did.

tips.title: Make It Personal
tips.content: You know this person. Reference your friendship, a memory of them with their partner, or something specific about their relationship that you admire.

tips.title: Match the Relationship
tips.content: Close friends deserve heartfelt messages. Casual friends might appreciate something lighter. Write in a voice they'd recognize as you.

tips.title: Look Forward
tips.content: Wedding cards are about the future. Wish them specific joys: laughter, adventures, someone to binge Netflix with. Make it real.

shortMessages: So happy for you both! Here's to a lifetime of love and laughter.
You two are perfect together. Congratulations on making it official!
Watching you find your person has been the best. So happy for you!
mediumMessages: Congratulations! From the first time you told me about [partner's name], I knew this one was different. So happy to see you this happy. Here's to forever.
You two just make sense. The way you look at each other, the way you make each other laugh—it's the real thing. Wishing you a lifetime of that magic.
I've watched your love story unfold, and I couldn't be happier for you. You deserve every bit of this joy. Congratulations to you both!
heartfeltMessages: There aren't many people in this world who get to find their person. You found yours, and I've had a front-row seat to the kind of love that makes you believe in love. I'm so proud of you and so happy for you both.

You're one of my favorite people marrying one of your favorite people, which makes this one of my favorite days. Thank you for letting me be part of it. Here's to your forever.

I've seen you through the bad dates, the heartbreaks, and the "I'm going to be single forever" rants. And now I get to see you marry the person who makes all of that worth it. I'm crying. Congratulations.
pages.whenToSend: Wedding cards should be sent or delivered around the wedding day. If attending the reception, bring your card with your gift or place it in the designated card box. If mailing, send it within a week of the wedding—to their home address, not the venue.

faqs.question: Should I include money or a check in the card?
faqs.answer: Cash or checks are perfectly appropriate wedding gifts, especially if that's what the couple prefers. Tuck it securely in the card. Most couples appreciate contributions toward their new life together.

faqs.question: What if I only know one half of the couple?
faqs.answer: Address the card to both, but it's okay if your message focuses more on your friend: "[Friend's name], I'm so happy for you both. [Partner's name] is lucky to have you—and clearly has great taste."

faqs.question: Can I write something funny?
faqs.answer: Absolutely—if that matches your friendship. A well-placed joke can make a card memorable. Just balance humor with a genuine sentiment so it doesn't read as dismissive of the occasion.

pages.title: Birthday Card Messages for a Friend
pages.metaTitle: Birthday Card Messages for a Best Friend | Prosepal
pages.metaDescription: Find heartfelt birthday card messages for your best friend. 10 examples from funny to sincere, plus tips for writing something they'll keep forever.
pages.intro: Your best friend's birthday is coming up, and "Happy Birthday!" just isn't going to cut it. This is someone who knows your coffee order, your deepest fears, and that embarrassing thing from high school. They deserve a card that matches the friendship. Here's how to write it.

tips.title: Inside Jokes Are Gold
tips.content: The best birthday cards for friends reference your shared history. That inside joke that only you two understand? Include it. They'll love it.

tips.title: Balance Humor and Heart
tips.content: Start with something funny if that's your dynamic, but end with something real. Let them know they matter to you—you can be sincere and still be you.

tips.title: Celebrate Them Specifically
tips.content: Don't just wish them a happy birthday—tell them what makes them worth celebrating. Be specific about the qualities you love.

shortMessages: Happy birthday to my favorite person to do nothing with. Here's to another year.
Another year of putting up with me. Thanks for that. Happy birthday!
You're the best friend a person could ask for. Happy birthday!
mediumMessages: Happy birthday to the person who knows all my secrets and still sticks around. That's either friendship or blackmail material, and either way, I'm grateful for you.
You're the friend I text when something good happens, something bad happens, or nothing happens at all. Basically, you're stuck with me. Happy birthday!
Another year older, another year of me being the younger friend. (You're welcome for that.) Happy birthday to my favorite person.
heartfeltMessages: Happy birthday to the person who's been there through everything—the highs, the lows, and all the random Tuesday night texts. I don't know what I did to deserve a friend like you, but I'm not questioning it. Love you always.
I don't say it enough, but you're one of the best things in my life. You show up, you listen, you make me laugh until I can't breathe. I hope this birthday is as amazing as you are. Love you.

Here's to another year of adventures, inside jokes, and being the kind of friends that people make movies about. (We're definitely the funny ones, not the dramatic ones.) Happy birthday. I love you more than I probably say.
You've seen me at my best and my worst, and you've chosen to stay for all of it. That's not nothing—that's everything. Happy birthday to my person. Here's to many more years of this.
pages.whenToSend: Make sure your card arrives on or before their birthday. If you're seeing them in person, bring it to the celebration. For long-distance friends, mail it a week early and follow up with a phone call or video chat on the actual day.

faqs.question: What if I'm bad at writing cards?
faqs.answer: The fact that you're trying means something. Even a short, genuine message matters more than a perfectly crafted impersonal one. Start with one true thing you appreciate about them.

faqs.question: Can I be too cheesy?

faqs.question: What about a long-distance friend?
faqs.answer: A card in the mail means extra because you took the time to send it. Mention missing them and maybe suggest plans to see each other soon.

tips.title: Keep It Simple
tips.content: You don't need a long message. For acquaintances, a few sincere sentences are appropriate and appreciated. Don't overthink it.

tips.title: Avoid False Intimacy
tips.content: Don't pretend to know how they feel or reference a closeness that doesn't exist. Simple acknowledgment of their loss is enough.

tips.title: Your Effort Matters
tips.content: The fact that you're sending a card at all says something. Many people avoid acknowledging loss because they don't know what to say. You're not doing that.

shortMessages: I'm sorry for your loss. Thinking of you during this difficult time.
Wishing you peace and comfort. My thoughts are with you.
I'm so sorry to hear about your loss. Take care of yourself.
mediumMessages: I was sorry to hear about your loss. Though we don't know each other well, I wanted you to know I'm thinking of you during this difficult time.
Please accept my sincere condolences. I hope you find comfort in the love of those around you during this time.
I'm sorry for your loss. I know words can't change anything, but I wanted you to know that I'm thinking of you and your family.
heartfeltMessages: I don't know you well, but I know that loss is loss, and it always hurts. I'm sorry you're going through this, and I'm thinking of you.
We may not be close, but I want you to know that your loss hasn't gone unnoticed. I'm holding space for you during this difficult time.
I wasn't sure whether to send a card, but I decided that even a few words are better than silence. I'm sorry for your loss, and I hope you feel the support around you.
I may not know the right words, but I wanted you to know that I'm thinking of you. I'm sorry for your loss, and I hope you find moments of peace in the days ahead.
pages.whenToSend: Send your sympathy card within a week or two of learning about the loss. Even for acquaintances, acknowledging their loss matters. If you're unsure whether to send one, err on the side of sending—receiving a simple card is never unwelcome during grief.

faqs.question: Should I send a card if I barely know them?
faqs.answer: Yes—if you're aware of their loss, a simple card shows you care. It doesn't require a deep relationship to offer genuine condolences.

faqs.question: What if I only know them through someone else?
faqs.answer: That's fine. You can mention the connection: "I heard about your loss through [mutual friend]. I wanted to let you know I'm thinking of you."

faqs.question: Is a card better than saying nothing?
faqs.answer: Almost always, yes. Grieving people often feel isolated when others avoid the topic. Even a brief acknowledgment can offer comfort.

tips.title: Share a Sibling Perspective

shortMessages: From annoying sibling to happily married—who saw that coming? Congratulations!
So happy for you both. Welcome to the family, [partner's name]!
My baby [brother/sister] is all grown up. I'm not crying. Congratulations!
mediumMessages: I've been there through the braces, the bad haircuts, and the questionable fashion phases. Now I get to be here for this—the best day yet. So proud of you. Congratulations!
Watching you find your person has been one of the best things. [Partner's name], you're officially family now, and we couldn't be happier about it. Welcome!
Who would've thought my [brother/sister] would be the one to figure out this whole love thing? I'm so happy for you both. Here's to your forever.

pages.whenToSend: Bring your card to the wedding and place it in the card box, or give it to your sibling privately if you want a more personal moment. You might also consider writing a second card for the rehearsal dinner if you're giving a speech—something just for them.

faqs.question: Should I share childhood stories in my card?

faqs.question: How do I address the card?
faqs.answer: Address it to both your sibling and their partner: "To [Sibling] and [Partner]" shows you're welcoming them as a couple.

faqs.question: What if I'm not close with my sibling's partner?

tips.title: Be Specific If You Can

faqs.question: What if they struggled to have this baby?

faqs.question: Should I include a gift?

faqs.question: What if I haven't met the baby yet?
faqs.answer: That's fine—express your excitement to meet them. "I can't wait to meet [baby's name] and give you all the biggest hugs. Congratulations!"

pages.intro: Your coworker is out sick or recovering, and you want to send something supportive. But how personal should you get? How do you acknowledge their situation without prying? Here's how to write a get well card that's warm without overstepping.

tips.title: Keep It Light Unless You're Close
tips.content: For casual coworker relationships, a warm but brief message is appropriate. Save the deeply personal notes for people you know well outside of work.

tips.title: Don't Pry Into Their Situation
tips.content: You don't need to know (or mention) specifics about their illness. "Hope you feel better soon" works for any situation.

tips.title: Offer to Help With Work
tips.content: One of the best things you can offer a recovering coworker is peace of mind about their workload. Let them know things are covered.

shortMessages: Hope you're feeling better soon! We miss you around here.
Wishing you a speedy recovery. Take all the time you need.
Get well soon! The office isn't the same without you.
mediumMessages: I hope you're resting and taking care of yourself. Don't worry about anything here—we've got it covered. Focus on getting better!
Wishing you a quick recovery! The team is thinking of you. Please don't hesitate to reach out if there's anything I can do.
Heard you're under the weather and wanted to send some good vibes. Take all the time you need—we'll hold down the fort until you're back.
heartfeltMessages: I know this hasn't been easy, and I just wanted you to know that we're all rooting for you. Focus on getting better—the rest can wait. We miss you and can't wait to see you back.

I know it's hard to be away, but please don't worry about anything here. Your health is what matters. We're all looking forward to seeing your smiling face again soon.

faqs.question: Should the whole team sign one card?
faqs.answer: A team card is great for general illnesses. For more serious or personal situations, individual cards from close coworkers may be more appropriate alongside a team card.

faqs.question: What if I don't know what they're going through?
faqs.answer: That's okay—keep it general. "Hope you're feeling better soon" works regardless of the situation. You don't need details to express genuine care.

faqs.question: Is it appropriate to send flowers or gifts?
faqs.answer: A team gift or flowers is nice for longer recoveries. Check with HR or close coworkers about preferences. Some people appreciate flowers; others prefer cards or meal deliveries.

tips.title: Offer Ongoing Support

heartfeltMessages: Losing [name] means losing your person—the one who knew you best, loved you most, and was supposed to be there for the rest of your life. I'm so deeply sorry. I can't fix this pain, but I can sit with you in it. I'm here.

faqs.question: What if they were together for a very long time?

faqs.question: Should I mention my own loss of a spouse?

faqs.question: How do I support them long-term?

Consider writing the card now and sending it when the timing feels right. Follow the card with consistent actions that prove you meant what you wrote.

faqs.question: What if they don't accept my apology?
faqs.answer: That's their right. You apologized for you—because it was the right thing to do. Whether or not they forgive you isn't something you can control. Give them space and time.

faqs.question: Should I give a gift with my apology?
faqs.answer: Be careful—a gift can feel like you're trying to "buy" forgiveness. If you want to include something, make it meaningful and personal rather than expensive. The apology itself is the important part.

faqs.question: How do I apologize if I'm not sure what I did wrong?
faqs.answer: Start by listening. Before writing a card, have a conversation (if they're willing) to understand their perspective. "Help me understand how I hurt you" is more powerful than a vague apology.

tips.content: Don't skip past the hard stuff with toxic positivity. Acknowledge that what they're facing is genuinely difficult before offering encouragement.

tips.title: Focus on Their Strengths
tips.content: Remind them of qualities they have that will help them through this. Be specific—"You're the strongest person I know" is nice, but "The way you handled [past situation] shows me you can handle this" is better.

tips.title: Offer Your Presence
tips.content: Sometimes the most encouraging thing is knowing someone's in your corner. Let them know you're there—not with empty offers, but with genuine availability.

shortMessages: I believe in you. Always have, always will.
You've got this. And when you feel like you don't, you've got me.
Rough times don't last. Strong people do. You're one of the strong ones.
mediumMessages: I know things are really hard right now, and I wish I could fix it for you. Since I can't, just know that I'm here. I believe in you completely, and I'm not going anywhere.
Life has thrown you a curveball, but if anyone can figure out how to catch it, it's you. You're stronger than you know. And you don't have to be strong alone—I'm right here.
I've watched you navigate hard things before, and you always come through. This time won't be different. Lean on me whenever you need to.
heartfeltMessages: I don't know the right words to say, but I know you—and I know you have everything you need inside you to get through this. Even when you can't see it, I can. I'm here, cheering you on and ready to catch you if you fall.

pages.whenToSend: Send an encouragement card whenever you learn your friend is struggling. Don't wait for the "right" moment—there isn't one. What matters is that they know you're thinking of them. Follow up in the weeks ahead; challenges don't resolve overnight.

faqs.question: What if I don't know what they're going through exactly?
faqs.answer: That's okay—you can still offer support. "I heard you're going through a hard time. I don't need to know the details to tell you I'm in your corner." Sometimes not knowing is fine.

faqs.question: Should I offer advice in my card?
faqs.answer: Usually no—unless they've specifically asked for advice. Most people facing challenges want support and acknowledgment more than solutions. Save advice for conversations where you can listen first.

faqs.question: How do I avoid sounding like a greeting card cliche?
faqs.answer: Be specific and personal. Reference their actual situation, actual strengths, and your actual relationship. Generic encouragement feels hollow; personalized encouragement feels real.

tips.title: Wish Them Well in What's Next
tips.content: Farewell cards should look forward. Wherever they're going, wish them success and happiness in their next chapter.

shortMessages: Best of luck on your new adventure! You'll be missed.

The office won't be the same without you. Good luck out there!

heartfeltMessages: I'm not going to lie—I'm really going to miss you. You've made work better, and not just because of your [skill/contribution]—because of who you are. Thank you for being a great colleague and an even better person. Your next team is lucky to have you.

faqs.question: Should the whole team sign one card?
faqs.answer: A team card is standard practice and appreciated. If you're particularly close, consider also giving a personal card with a more meaningful message.

faqs.question: What if I don't know them well?
faqs.answer: Keep it brief and warm: "Best of luck in your new role! It was nice working with you." You don't need a deep relationship to offer genuine well-wishes.
